fact_1: Each Dove is a 3U CubeSat of about 5 kg and 10 x 10 x 34 cm.
fact_2: Its camera images land at 3 to 5 m resolution from sun-synchronous orbit.
fact_3: Planet built its own X-band radio because image volume was the bottleneck; its first downlink in 2013 ran at 4 Mbps.
why_it_resembles_your_design: Like Doves, your spacecraft is a CubeSat whose useful output is limited by how much imagery it can send to the ground.

fact_1: Each satellite weighs about 85 to 110 kg and carries an X-band radar that images day or night through cloud.
fact_2: The radar's peak radiated power is 3.2 kW, far more than the satellite's solar panels make on average, so it images for only a short part of each orbit.
fact_3: It sends data down at 140 Mbps (500 Mbps on later models) in X-band and uses ion propulsion to maintain its orbit.
why_it_resembles_your_design: Like ICEYE, your radar draws more power than the panels supply, so battery size and imaging time are the central trade-off.

fact_1: It launched on 18 June 2009 on an Atlas V 401 at 1,916 kg, of which 1,018 kg was dry mass, so nearly half was propellant.
fact_2: Its science payload had a mass of 92.6 kg, and its solar array supplied about 1,850 W at end of life.
fact_3: Its cameras image the Moon at about 0.5 m per pixel from a 50 km orbit.
why_it_resembles_your_design: Like LRO, your orbiter must carry a large share of its launch mass as fuel to enter and hold a low lunar orbit.
